subject: MAP: Technical evaluation — benchmark criteria & shortlist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthgrid.com>, Samira Patel <samira.patel@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation — benchmark criteria & shortlist

Hi Liam / Samira —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed MAP milestone for the technical evaluation so we can align on success criteria, owners, and timing. I captured the minimum viable benchmark for your engineering team to validate performance and unit economics for the primary use case you described (customer support summarization + context-aware suggestions).

Proposed MAP milestone: Technical evaluation run
- Target close: 2026-04-09 (3 weeks)
- Objective: Confirm model+config that meets latency, cost, and quality thresholds for production traffic pattern
- Success criteria (must pass all):
  * Latency: P95 generation latency <= 180ms for 1-2k token responses on 8xA100-equivalent run (simulated concurrency 50 RPS)
  * Quality: ROUGE-L / pairwise preference > current baseline by >= 6% on the provided evaluation set (HealthGrid-support-50k)
  * Cost: token-in/token-out unit cost <= $0.40 per 1k effective tokens at observed throughput after batching and caching strategies
  * Stability: no more than 0.5% error rate (timeouts / OOM) across a 2-hour steady-state test

Milestone responsibilities / owners
- HealthGrid: provide representative eval dataset (export or shared Drive link) and a contact for infra coordination (Samira for procurement/access) — due 2026-03-22
- Redwood (Marissa): coordinate benchmark schedule, secure test capacity, and provide MAP document — due 2026-03-20
- Redwood (Jordan / Diego): propose a model shortlist, runbook, and run the benchmark — runbook & shortlist due 2026-03-24; benchmark execution 2026-03-25–03-27

Dependencies / blockers
- Dataset delivery and any IP redaction requirements from your side
- Access to an account/VM for load testing (we can run in Redwood sandbox if preferred)

Attachments: MAP-draft-technical-eval-v1.xlsx (attached) — this is a simple milestone table I started.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the target close date (2026-04-09) and dataset handoff date (2026-03-22)?
2) Are there any hard constraints on models (no LLMs that retain logs, on-prem only, etc.)?
3) Who should we add to the bench run coordination (ops/infra lead)?

I'll loop Jordan/Diego to draft the shortlist and runbook once you confirm.

Best,

--
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation — benchmark criteria & shortlist — runbook + shortlist

Thanks Marissa — sketching the runbook and shortlist below. Diego and I will produce the runbook doc and the model-cost CSV by EOD today. High-level plan:

Benchmark runbook (high level)
1) Ingest HealthGrid-support-50k into our eval harness (anonymize PII according to their retention rules)
2) Warm KV cache with realistic prefixes from the dataset (to simulate conversational cache hits)
3) Run steady-state traffic generator at 50 RPS for 2 hours with concurrency patterns matched to their production profile
4) Measure: token-level throughput, P50/P95/P99 generation latency, model CPU/GPU memory footprint, error rates, and cost estimate computed from observed token/sec and instance-hour costs
5) Post-process: compute ROUGE-L and pairwise preference using the labeled subset (HealthGrid-annotations-1k)

Model shortlist (initial, 3 flavors each where applicable):
- Llama 2 13B (q4f, q8) — low latency, good quality for our prompt templates; expected to hit cost target with q4f on batching
- Llama 2 70B (q8) — highest quality; risk: higher memory and potential OOM without KV-splitting; expect higher infra cost
- Falcon 40B Instruct (q8/q4f) — strong latency/cost tradeoff, good for instruction-heavy summaries
- Mistral 7B Instruct (q4f) — baseline fast option for low-cost deployment
- Redwood-verified-small (open-checkpoint 16B q8) — our curated config that often balances quality and latency (included as a candidate)

Quantization & infra notes:
- Start with q8 and q4f variants where available; q4f tends to reduce GPU memory and improve throughput at small quality cost
- Use 8xA100-equivalent pool for the steady-state run; we can simulate lower-cost instance types if HealthGrid requests

Expected quick estimates (very rough)
- Llama2-13B q4f: ~P95 120–160ms at 50 RPS; est cost ~$0.18–0.26 / 1k tokens
- Falcon-40B q8: ~P95 140–190ms; est cost ~$0.22–0.35 / 1k tokens
- Llama2-70B q8: ~P95 200–270ms; est cost ~$0.45+ / 1k tokens (may fail cost target)

Responsibilities & timeline
- Jordan: lead runbook + measurement scripts (deliverable benchmark-runbook.md) — due 2026-03-20 EOD
- Diego: cost modeling and infra coordination; prepare model-shortlist.csv with per-model cost estimates — due 2026-03-20 EOD
- Marissa: confirm dataset delivery and retention constraints with HealthGrid; coordinate schedule for execution

I'll attach the initial runbook and CSV. If we see Llama2-70B missing the cost target, we'll propose Redwood-verified-small or aggressive q4f to meet the bar.

-Jordan

Attachments: benchmark-runbook.md (draft), model-shortlist.csv
